title: Cost of completion and loss in value
shortTitle: Cost of completion and loss in value
summary: These measures compare the cost of obtaining the promised performance with the reduction in the property’s value caused by the defect. The governing rule decides which better protects the contractual entitlement in the circumstances.
notes:
Plante evaluates substantial construction and the cost of correcting particular deficiencies. Groves and Peevyhouse reach different results about restorative work whose cost greatly exceeded the resulting market-value increase. The significance of the promise, the character of the breach, proportionality, and the court’s understanding of the contract matter.

Cost of completion is not automatically a windfall merely because the owner has not yet done the work. Loss in value is not automatically adequate merely because it is cheaper for the breacher. Identify the interest the promise protected, the evidence of valuation and cost, and the legal limits the relevant court applied. Preserve dissents and procedural outcomes rather than converting these cases into a single arithmetic formula.

textbookImport.basis: Plain-language synthesis of the cited casebook passages; subject to the jurisdictional and source limits stated there.

topics.damages-cost-value: The cases compare the cost of obtaining performance with reduced value.
